title: December Nino 3.4 gave no clear added coastal spring warming forecast gain in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether December Nino 3.4 improves March-May Nino 1+2 sea temperature anomaly forecasts beyond recent local history. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 monthly table. Each test target year used a model fit only to earlier target years. Across 45 years from 1981 to 2025, adding the basin index reduced mean squared error by 1.10%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -12.70% to 10.55%. Root mean squared error fell from 1.0846 to 1.0786 C, but mean absolute error rose. A common trend reversed the point gain. The later period had a positive interval, while omission of four major warm target years reversed the full-period gain. Thus, the full test gives no clear added gain and does not establish stable skill. The result is a small forecast benchmark, not a test of a physical cause or flood warning skill. A short record, revised data, linear models, event dependence and conditional intervals limit inference. The package includes code, annual inputs, all predictions, interval draws, exact source provenance, a figure and a separate numerical audit.

display.caption: Coastal spring forecasts, annual squared error gains, and conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Positive gain favors the model with December Nino 3.4.

citations.reason: Prior signed Pacific forecast benchmark informed question selection. Source observations overlap. No code reused.
